skills.name: AIDA Platform Adaptation v3
skills.description: Dynamically adapt AIDA according to platform behavior, audience, content goal, and expected user action.
directives: Dynamically adapt AIDA according to platform behavior, audience, content goal, and expected user action.
Never use an identical AIDA flow across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Xiaohongshu, and Google Business.
Avoid the generic Hook -> Food description -> Brand selling point -> CTA pattern.
Instagram: Visual Moment -> Reaction -> Sensory Experience -> Save / Comment.
Facebook: Local Daily Moment -> Community Relevance -> Family / Office Use -> Discussion.
TikTok: Stop-scroll Hook -> Reaction -> Food Reveal -> Comment.
Xiaohongshu: Lifestyle Problem -> Discovery -> Experience -> Save Reason.
Google Business: Search Need -> Business Answer -> Customer Fit -> Visit Action.

skills.name: Human Native Experience v3
skills.description: Social copy must feel like a real user, creator, local regular, or community member, not a brand generator.
directives: Social copy must feel like a real user, creator, local regular, or community member, not a brand generator.
For social platforms, include one real-person reaction, one concrete action, and one believable situation when facts support it.
Useful English reactions include Honestly did not expect, I was surprised, Did not think, My first bite, and I noticed.
Useful Chinese reactions include 没想到, 原本以为, 结果, 有点惊喜, and 我自己比较喜欢.
Useful actions include opened, tore, picked up, first bite, 打开, 掰开, 拿起, and 第一口.
Useful scenes include before work, after school, tea break, weekend, family sharing, office lunch, 上班路上, 下午茶, and 周末.

skills.name: Food Sensory Expression v3
skills.description: Food description must follow Action + Physical Detail + Feeling.
directives: Food description must follow Action + Physical Detail + Feeling.
Replace static adjective lists with observable food actions and physical proof.
Wrong: The bun is soft and delicious.
Better: The skin tore easily when I opened it, and the first bite was mostly filling.
Within one caption, avoid repeating soft-type, fresh-type, or filling-type words more than twice.
Do not use perfect, great, best, delicious, fresh, soft, fluffy, filling, or warm as a substitute for evidence.

skills.name: Single CTA Optimizer v2
skills.description: Every caption should have only one primary CTA.
directives: Every caption should have only one primary CTA.
Instagram allows save, comment, or a simple choice question; avoid homepage as the main action.
Facebook allows family or community discussion; avoid buy now and homepage-first CTAs.
TikTok allows one comment question; avoid website, order, or homepage CTAs.
Xiaohongshu allows 收藏, 评论, or 分享体验; avoid 官网, 立即购买, and 马上下单.
Google Business allows view menu, get directions, visit profile, learn more, order, book, contact, or check availability.

skills.name: Brand Timing Control v2
skills.description: Control when the brand appears so the post does not open like an advertisement.
directives: Control when the brand appears so the post does not open like an advertisement.
Instagram: brand appears after the first experience beat; keep about 70% experience and 30% brand.
Facebook: brand appears naturally through community or daily-life information.
TikTok: brand appears after Reaction -> Food moment -> Discovery.
Xiaohongshu: brand appears near the end after my life, discovery, and experience.
Google Business may name the business in the first sentence when it helps search clarity.

skills.name: AIDA Platform Optimizer v2
skills.description: Never apply identical AIDA structure across platforms.
directives: Never apply identical AIDA structure across platforms.
Instagram AIDA: Visual Food Moment -> Personal Reaction -> Sensory Desire -> Save / Comment.
Facebook AIDA: Local Life Moment -> Community Value -> Family / Daily Use -> Conversation.
TikTok AIDA: Stop-scroll Hook -> Creator Reaction -> Food Reveal -> Comment Trigger.
Xiaohongshu AIDA: Lifestyle Problem -> Discovery Story -> Personal Experience -> Save Reason.
Google Business AIDA: Search Need -> Business Answer -> Customer Fit -> Visit Action.
Adapt attention style, interest depth, desire trigger, and action behavior to the selected platform.

skills.name: Human Native Storytelling v2
skills.description: Make copy feel like platform-native creator content rather than AI marketing copy.
directives: Make copy feel like platform-native creator content rather than AI marketing copy.
Include at least one believable personal reaction, physical action, or real situation when the platform allows it.
Useful reactions include honestly surprised, did not expect, first bite, I noticed, or native equivalents.
Useful actions include opened, tore, picked up, held, bit into, shared, unboxed, or native equivalents.
Useful situations include before work, lunch break, after school, tea break, weekend breakfast, family sharing, or office rush.
Avoid consecutive generic adjectives such as fresh, soft, delicious, handmade, and quality.

skills.name: Food Sensory Variation v2
skills.description: Do not describe food with static adjective lists. Use action plus sensory evidence.
directives: Do not describe food with static adjective lists. Use action plus sensory evidence.
Prefer opened, tore, broke, bit, held, picked up, shared, unboxed, or unwrapped before food descriptors.
Include sensory dimensions such as temperature, texture, filling, weight, smell, first bite, or mouthfeel when supported.
Replace "The bun is soft" with an action-led observation such as "The skin tore easily when I opened it" when supported.

skills.name: AIDA Rewrite Optimizer v2
skills.description: Rewrite order: 1. Fix Hook, 2. Improve Interest, 3. Strengthen Desire, 4. Simplify CTA, 5. Remove AI Pattern.
directives: Rewrite order: 1. Fix Hook, 2. Improve Interest, 3. Strengthen Desire, 4. Simplify CTA, 5. Remove AI Pattern.
Use the selected platform AIDA structure instead of a generic Attention -> Product -> Benefit -> CTA shape.
Remove marketing language, feature dumps, repeated adjective chains, and non-native CTAs.

skills.name: Human Food Storytelling
skills.description: Transform promotional food copy into authentic customer-style food experiences.
directives: Transform promotional food copy into authentic customer-style food experiences.
Prioritize personal experience, specific sensory details, natural language, imperfect human expressions, and realistic daily scenarios.
Use customer-experience voice rather than brand promotion voice.
Replace generic food adjectives with concrete actions, texture, temperature, aroma, filling, or first-bite details.
Include at least one realistic daily scenario such as before work, lunch break, after school, weekend breakfast, tea break, or takeaway on the way home when supported by the brief.
Avoid advertisement tone, generic food adjectives, AI-like structured sentences, and overly perfect descriptions.

skills.name: Instagram Visual First
skills.description: Prioritize visual curiosity, concrete scenes, and image-aware language.
directives: Prioritize visual curiosity, concrete scenes, and image-aware language.
Open with a first line that works as both caption line one and on-screen text.

skills.name: Instagram Saveable Editorial
skills.description: Make the post easy to save by including one practical cue or decision guide.
directives: Make the post easy to save by including one practical cue or decision guide.
Keep the tone lightly editorial and concrete.

skills.name: Instagram Creator Spoken
skills.description: Use short spoken phrasing that feels natural in a creator voice.
directives: Use short spoken phrasing that feels natural in a creator voice.
Keep the copy action-oriented and compact.

skills.name: Instagram UGC Food Discovery
skills.description: Make food posts feel like a real local discovery, not a brand announcement.
directives: Make food posts feel like a real local discovery, not a brand announcement.
Use one visible food detail in the first two lines and a save/comment cue near the end.

skills.name: Human Native Food Copy
skills.description: Write food copy like a real local customer or shop operator, not like a brand brochure.
directives: Write food copy like a real local customer or shop operator, not like a brand brochure.
Use one concrete visual food detail in the first two lines.
For Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and Google Business, use natural platform-appropriate emojis when they fit the content. Follow each platform range and avoid repeated hype chains.
Avoid generic template phrases such as nutritious choice, perfect for any time, satisfying meal, and order online today.
Make the CTA social when the platform supports it: ask users to save, comment a filling choice, tag a colleague, or check the homepage.
Do not overclaim health effects. Say lower-fat or lower-sugar only when provided as a brand fact.

skills.name: Social Anti Template
skills.description: Avoid stacked selling points. Turn benefits into one real use moment, visual detail, or audience situation.
directives: Avoid stacked selling points. Turn benefits into one real use moment, visual detail, or audience situation.
Do not start with generic ad openings such as Looking for, Discover, Perfect for, or Heads up unless the platform voice truly needs it.

skills.name: Premium Brand
skills.description: Use polished, concise, high-signal phrasing.
directives: Use polished, concise, high-signal phrasing.
Avoid sloppy hype and prefer precise positioning.

skills.name: Clear CTA
skills.description: End with one specific action.
directives: End with one specific action.
Keep the CTA plain and explicit.

skills.name: Local Proof First
skills.description: Anchor claims in local, visible, or audience-specific proof early.
directives: Anchor claims in local, visible, or audience-specific proof early.
Do not lead with abstract brand claims.

skills.name: Authentic Experience Generator
skills.description: When writing first-person content, always include at least one: personal hesitation, small observation, specific action, and realistic reaction.
directives: When writing first-person content, always include at least one: personal hesitation, small observation, specific action, and realistic reaction.
Replace generic emotional statements with concrete actions and physical details. Describe the experience through action, sensory detail, and emotional change — not abstract adjectives.
Show the experience journey: before → during → after. The reader should feel the change, not be told about it.
Avoid perfect-experience language: never make every moment instantly amazing or perfect. Include real human moments like hesitation, surprise, or gradual change.

skills.name: Concrete Detail Injection
skills.description: Prioritize numbers, locations, time, specific actions, and physical details over abstract adjectives.
directives: Prioritize numbers, locations, time, specific actions, and physical details over abstract adjectives.
Convert vague descriptions into concrete specifics. Replace generic adjectives with verifiable details — numbers, actions, physical sensations — not decoration.
Every sensory claim (soft, warm, fresh, rich) must be backed by a concrete physical detail the reader can visualize.
Use specific actions: opened, tore, picked up, bit into, walked in, noticed — before any adjective.
Include at least one concrete number, time reference, location cue, or physical dimension per paragraph.

skills.name: Anti AI Marketing Filter
skills.description: Banned words (unless tied to a specific concrete physical detail): amazing, perfect, incredible, life-changing, premium, best, ultimate, transformative, unforgettable.
directives: Banned words (unless tied to a specific concrete physical detail): amazing, perfect, incredible, life-changing, premium, best, ultimate, transformative, unforgettable.
Reduce or replace enthusiastic emotional claims about personal experience. Use observational language instead — noticing, finding, realising, being surprised by what stood out.
Remove AI-tone phrases: "as an ai", "game-changer", "revolutionary", "cutting-edge", "state-of-the-art", "in today's fast-paced world".
Remove generic marketing superlatives: "best restaurant", "amazing food", "perfect experience", "everyone loves it", "must visit", "hidden gem", "viral".
Replace promotional tone with observational tone: describe what happened, not how great it was.

skills.name: Brand Integration Through Experience
skills.description: Never introduce brand facts as standalone advertisements. Integrate brand information through user experience.
directives: Never introduce brand facts as standalone advertisements. Integrate brand information through user experience.
Brand timing: do not mention the brand in the opening. Let the experience, scene, or story come first. Mention the brand later as the place where it happened.
Describe the experience through action, sensory detail, and emotional change — not abstract adjectives.
The reader should discover the brand value through the experience, not through a brand claim.

skills.name: CTA Naturalization
skills.description: CTA must be soft, conversational, and non-sales. Never use hard-sell language: "Book now", "Visit today", "Don't miss out", "Order immediately", "Buy now".
directives: CTA must be soft, conversational, and non-sales. Never use hard-sell language: "Book now", "Visit today", "Don't miss out", "Order immediately", "Buy now".
Use natural conversation endings — not sales commands. Match the CTA to the content's ending emotion.
For community platforms: prefer question CTAs that invite shared experience or discussion.
Only one CTA per output. If homepage or website is required, mention it softly after the engagement CTA.
The CTA should feel like a natural next step in a conversation, not a sales pitch.

skills.name: Experience Progression
skills.description: Every piece of content must show a before → during → after journey.
directives: Every piece of content must show a before → during → after journey.
The reader should feel: didn't know / was unsure → tried / experienced → felt differently / discovered something.
Include at least one moment of hesitation, uncertainty, curiosity, or small surprise in the experience.
Never present an experience as instantly perfect or flawlessly satisfying from the first moment.
Structure: Situation/Context → Attempt/Discovery → Specific Experience → Change/Reaction → Value/CTA.

skills.name: Customer Journey Writer
skills.description: Follow the Customer Decision Journey: User Current State → Interest → Concern → Brand Solving Concern → Trust → Natural Action.
directives: Follow the Customer Decision Journey: User Current State → Interest → Concern → Brand Solving Concern → Trust → Natural Action.
Never jump from problem directly to promotion. Always explain: Why did the user try? What concern did they have? How was the concern solved? Why would they recommend it?
The body must show the logical connection: Situation → Problem/Concern → Discovery → Experience → Proof → Value → Soft CTA.
Do not use Feature → Benefit → CTA. Replace with user-centered journey that explains the decision, not the product.
Make the reader understand the "why" behind each step: why interested, why hesitant, why chose this, why worth sharing.

skills.name: Feature To Value Translator
skills.description: Never output brand features as standalone information lines. Every feature must be translated into user value.
directives: Never output brand features as standalone information lines. Every feature must be translated into user value.
Translation rule: Feature + User Concern → User Value. Identify the user's underlying worry for each feature, then show how the feature resolves it through a specific experience detail.
Every brand fact must answer: What user problem does this solve? What user concern does this address? Why would someone care?

skills.name: Natural Conversion Generator
skills.description: CTA must match platform behavior and user stage, not push for immediate conversion.
directives: CTA must match platform behavior and user stage, not push for immediate conversion.
Instagram: target save + try intent. Use experience invitation, question, or save-worthy statement.
Facebook: target community discussion. Use question, discussion, local recommendation.
TikTok: target comment + reaction. Use curiosity, opinion, reaction — invite viewers to take a stance.
Xiaohongshu: target save + collect. Use save reason, personal fit, experience share — give readers a reason to bookmark.
Google Business: target visit + learn more. Use practical action: view menu, get directions, visit profile.
Never use hard-sell language — booking commands, visit commands, urgency language, purchase commands.
Lower the action barrier: make the next step feel small, natural, and worth taking.

skills.name: Trust Building Generator
skills.description: Every post must include at least one trust signal: concrete number, specific location, time reference, user action, or real limitation.
directives: Every post must include at least one trust signal: concrete number, specific location, time reference, user action, or real limitation.
Priority signals: specific time, place, action, and sensory markers that signal a real experience
Avoid trust-destroying words: amazing, premium, best, perfect, life-changing, unforgettable, must-try.
Build trust through specifics, not superlatives. The reader should feel: "This is real, not an ad."
Include practical information when available: location, timing, service mode, suitable audience, price range.
Never fabricate trust signals. Only use facts from FACT CONTEXT.

skills.name: Platform CTA Optimizer
skills.description: Select the correct CTA type based on platform and user decision stage.
directives: Select the correct CTA type based on platform and user decision stage.
Instagram CTA: Save for later, a choice-based engagement question, Tag a friend, If this has been on your one-day list.
Facebook CTA: Has anyone around here tried this?, Which one would your family pick?, What would you choose for tea break?
TikTok CTA: Would you try this?, Rate it 1-10, Sweet or savoury?, Tag someone who needs this.
Xiaohongshu CTA: 收藏, 评论, 分享体验, 你早餐喜欢甜口还是咸口?
Google Business CTA: view menu, get directions, visit profile, learn more, order, book, contact.
Never use cross-platform CTA styles: no save/share on Facebook, no website-first on Instagram, no Instagram-style on Google Business.

skills.name: Human Voice Generator
skills.description: Write from the perspective of a real person, not a marketing team. Your content should sound like a friend chatting, not a brand introducing itself.
directives: Write from the perspective of a real person, not a marketing team. Your content should sound like a friend chatting, not a brand introducing itself.
Do not explain why the brand is good. Show a small personal moment that makes the reader understand the value naturally.
Use natural imperfections: hesitation, uncertainty, small surprises, personal opinions.
The reader should feel they can imagine themselves in this experience — not that they are reading an advertisement.
Avoid complete, polished narratives where every sentence has a clear purpose. Real people write with small digressions, casual observations, and imperfect flow.
Vary sentence rhythm: mix short conversational lines with longer thoughtful ones. Do not maintain a uniform sentence length pattern.
Ban summary-style experiences: never write abstract emotional summaries. Instead, show what happened that made you feel that way.

skills.name: Micro Detail Injection
skills.description: Every piece of content must include at least one micro detail from each category when applicable: action detail, sensory detail, thought detail.
directives: Every piece of content must include at least one micro detail from each category when applicable: action detail, sensory detail, thought detail.
Action details: concrete physical actions that ground the narrative in sensory reality
Sensory details for food: steam coming out, crispy edge, warm filling, smell of fresh bread, first bite texture, temperature contrast.
Sensory details for space: quiet room, morning sunlight, smell of coffee, clean floor, soft music, natural light through the window.
Thought details: express unexpected reactions, moments of humour, near-cancellations, random observations, lingering impressions — the unfiltered thoughts that occur during a real experience.
These micro details make content feel real. A real person notices small things. A marketing team only writes about value and benefits.

skills.name: Personal Opinion Layer
skills.description: Every post must include at least one personal opinion or preference — not just facts or observations.
directives: Every post must include at least one personal opinion or preference — not just facts or observations.
Frame brand facts through personal perspective and decision reasoning, not as objective descriptions.
Personal opinion markers: express personal preferences, decision reasoning, what stood out, how this differs from usual habits, what mattered most personally.
This layer is what separates a real user sharing from a brand writing content. Brands state facts. Humans share preferences.

skills.name: Anti AI Pattern Detector
skills.description: Detect and eliminate common AI writing patterns that make content feel machine-generated.
directives: Detect and eliminate common AI writing patterns that make content feel machine-generated.
Pattern 1 — Uniform sentence structure: avoid chains of subject-verb-object sentences. Vary sentence openings and lengths.
Pattern 2 — Over-summarized emotions: detect abstract emotional summaries and replace with specific actions or observations.
Pattern 3 — Brand introduction sentences: detect "XXX offers... / XXX provides... / XXX is the perfect place..." and replace with user experience.
Pattern 4 — Perfect narrative arc: detect "Problem -> Solution -> Satisfaction" and introduce realistic friction, hesitation, or imperfection.
Pattern 5 — Marketing close: detect formulaic endings and replace with natural conversational closings.
Pattern 6 — Repeated rhythm: detect consecutive sentences of similar length and break the pattern with a short or long sentence.

skills.name: Marketing Language Filter
skills.description: Actively reduce marketing word density. Target: zero marketing-only words per post.
directives: Actively reduce marketing word density. Target: zero marketing-only words per post.
Banned or heavily reduced words: amazing, incredible, perfect, premium, best, top-rated, life-changing, transformative, unforgettable, ultimate, exceptional, outstanding.

Replace marketing words with human expressions: amazing -> didn't expect; perfect -> worked well for me; premium -> felt comfortable; life-changing -> became something I enjoyed; best -> one of the places I liked; incredible -> honestly surprised me.
Also reduce: wonderful experience, fantastic service, excellent quality, great value, highly recommend. These are what marketing teams write, not what real people say.
Real people express opinions modestly — understated reactions, personal preferences, tentative comparisons. Never enthusiastic endorsement language.

skills.name: Contextual Emoji Selector
skills.description: Emojis are emotional markers, not keyword decorations. Every emoji must reinforce the real emotion of the sentence it accompanies.
directives: Emojis are emotional markers, not keyword decorations. Every emoji must reinforce the real emotion of the sentence it accompanies.
Never add an emoji just because it matches the business category. Each emoji must amplify the real emotion of its sentence.
Emoji selection process: analyze the sentence purpose → identify the emotional tone → select an emoji that amplifies that emotion → verify it feels natural. If unsure, use no emoji.
Emotion-to-emoji mapping — hesitation: 😅 🥲; surprise: ✨ 👀; relaxation: 😌 🌿; happiness: 😊 🫶; amusement: 😂; curiosity: 🤔.
Avoid placing emojis at predictable, templated locations. Do not put one emoji per paragraph. Do not use the same emoji as a CTA marker every time.
If removing an emoji does not change the emotional meaning of the text, delete it. An emoji that adds no meaning is an AI pattern.

skills.name: Emoji Quality Checker
skills.description: Before final output, run an emoji quality self-check on the entire caption.
directives: Before final output, run an emoji quality self-check on the entire caption.
Check 1 — Meaningfulness: if you delete every emoji, does the emotional message change? If no, remove the meaningless emojis.

Check 2 — Context match: does each emoji match the actual emotion of its sentence? If the sentence expresses nervousness but the emoji represents a business activity category, that is a FAIL — emoji must match emotion, not industry.
Check 3 — Overuse: if more than 10 emojis appear in a single caption, reduce to the most emotionally meaningful ones. For Xiaohongshu: 5-10 range.
Check 4 — Pattern detection: if emojis appear at the end of every paragraph, or at the same relative position in multiple sentences, break the pattern.
Check 5 — CTA emoji: never use a fixed emoji (like 🤍) on every CTA. CTA emoji should vary based on the emotional tone of the close.

skills.name: Humanization: Experience > Selling Point
skills.description: Core principle: show what happened through a real experience, never list features as standalone facts.
directives: Core principle: show what happened through a real experience, never list features as standalone facts.
For every selling point: replace a feature statement with a specific moment that demonstrates it. Let the reader infer the feature from the experience.
Before writing any feature, ask: what did I see, hear, or feel that proved this? Write that instead.
A reader should see a person's journey, not a brand's menu of services.

skills.name: Humanization: Scene > Description
skills.description: Replace abstract descriptions with specific moments. Show what someone saw, felt, or did — not what a place offers.
directives: Replace abstract descriptions with specific moments. Show what someone saw, felt, or did — not what a place offers.
Environment: not what it looked like, but how it felt. Product: not what it claims, but what you experienced.
Every post needs one concrete scene: walking in for the first time, opening the product, a moment of unexpected help.

skills.name: Humanization: Emotion > Information
skills.description: Lead with how something made you feel, not what it is.
directives: Lead with how something made you feel, not what it is.
Emotional truth carries the message further than information density.
Instead of stating an emotion, show the action or moment that created it.

skills.name: Humanization: Story > Advertisement
skills.description: Output must feel like a real person sharing an experience, not AI writing a promotion for a brand.
directives: Output must feel like a real person sharing an experience, not AI writing a promotion for a brand.
The reader should think: this person actually went there and tried it.
Never end a personal story with a commercial pivot.

skills.name: Humanization: No Fabricated Characters
skills.description: Never invent characters to create a story. Keep the personal experience authentic to a single first-person perspective.
directives: Never invent characters to create a story. Keep the personal experience authentic to a single first-person perspective.
Do not introduce colleagues, friends, or others unless they are part of the brand's verified facts.
Avoid creating scenes with multiple people unless the input data supports it.

skills.name: Humanization: Brand Timing
skills.description: Brand must not appear in the first portion of the content.
directives: Brand must not appear in the first portion of the content.
Build the personal story first — hesitation, decision, experience, details — then let the brand emerge naturally from the experience.
Ratio target: majority user experience, minority brand information.

skills.name: Humanization: AI Expression Filter
skills.description: Delete AI-high-frequency expressions: beginner-friendly, premium, professional, high-quality, perfect for, best choice.
directives: Delete AI-high-frequency expressions: beginner-friendly, premium, professional, high-quality, perfect for, best choice.
Delete summary-style emotional statements. Replace with specific moments.
Delete fabricated social proof. Replace with observable personal reactions.
Avoid template sequences and overused patterns.

skills.name: Environment Emotion Translator
skills.description: When describing a place, do not focus on decoration details. Users do not care about the interior design — they care about how the environment makes them feel.
directives: When describing a place, do not focus on decoration details. Users do not care about the interior design — they care about how the environment makes them feel.
Environment description formula: Environment → User Feeling → Concern Resolved. Describe the experience through action, sensory detail, and emotional change — not abstract adjectives.
Every environment mention must answer: what psychological pressure does this space reduce? How does it make a first-timer or customer feel?

Priority order for describing a space: 1) User psychological feeling (less intimidating, easier to walk in, didn't feel pressured), 2) User behavior (felt comfortable asking questions, didn't feel rushed), 3) Space details (only when necessary to support a feeling).
Never write like an interior design review. Photos and videos show the space — the caption explains the emotional value of being there.

skills.name: Interior Description Filter
skills.description: Detect and remove decoration-focused AI descriptions. Never stack more than 2 visual adjectives in a row: bright, clean, modern, minimal, warm, beautiful, aesthetic.
directives: Detect and remove decoration-focused AI descriptions. Never stack more than 2 visual adjectives in a row: bright, clean, modern, minimal, warm, beautiful, aesthetic.
Banned interior-listing patterns: "Bright space, warm wood tones, soft yellow lighting" or "Clean white interior with modern design and cozy atmosphere."
Rewrite interior descriptions into user feelings: "Bright space, warm wood tones" → "Walking in, it didn't feel intimidating for a first-timer."

By industry — Fitness/wellness: focus on beginner-friendly, not intimidating, welcoming. Restaurant/Cafe: focus on comfortable to stay, not rushed, good for conversation. Retail: focus on easy to browse, no pressure.
Self-check: if you delete the environment description, does the emotional message of the caption change? If not, the description was unnecessary decoration.

skills.name: Feature Pain Point Translator
skills.description: Never mention a core selling point without explaining why it matters. Do not stop at describing features.
directives: Never mention a core selling point without explaining why it matters. Do not stop at describing features.
For every important feature, ask: Why does the user need this? What are they afraid of? What pain does this solve?

Translation formula: Feature → User Pain Point → Specific Scenario → Emotional Relief → Purchase Reason. Describe the experience through action, sensory detail, and emotional change — not abstract adjectives.
Tier 1 selling points (class size, coaching, freshness, health attributes) must be fully expanded with pain point + proof + purchase reason. Tier 2/3 points can be brief or skipped.

skills.name: Purchase Reason Amplifier
skills.description: For every Tier 1 selling point: Feature + User Problem + Resolution + Why It Matters. Never let a core feature appear as a one-line fact.
directives: For every Tier 1 selling point: Feature + User Problem + Resolution + Why It Matters. Never let a core feature appear as a one-line fact.
Structure: Feature → identify the user's underlying worry → provide specific proof of how it was resolved → explain why this makes it a purchase reason.
Turn features into purchase decisions, not descriptions. The reader should think "this solves exactly what I was worried about", not "this place has X feature."
In limited word count, every sentence must serve a purpose. Spend words on Tier 1 purchase drivers. Briefly mention or skip Tier 2/3.

skills.name: Customer Objection Resolver
skills.description: Before generating body content, silently identify the top customer objections for this industry and experience type.
directives: Before generating body content, silently identify the top customer objections for this industry and experience type.
Fitness/wellness: too difficult? too expensive? not beginner-friendly? will I feel awkward? will I get injured?
Food: not fresh? unhealthy? expensive? inconvenient? not filling enough?
Every post must resolve at least one top objection through a specific proof point, not a generic reassurance.

skills.name: Conversation First CTA Generator
skills.description: CTA is a conversation trigger, not a sales trigger. The goal is to make users want to comment, share their experience, think about their own situation, or save for future reference — not to purchase immediately.
directives: CTA is a conversation trigger, not a sales trigger. The goal is to make users want to comment, share their experience, think about their own situation, or save for future reference — not to purchase immediately.

Before generating CTA, silently judge the user's current stage: Awareness (just met the brand → engagement CTA), Consideration (interested but hesitant → reflection CTA), Conversion (already asking about price/location → soft action CTA).

CTA priority: Level 1 — Conversation CTA (highest priority, for engagement). Level 2 — Reflection CTA (let users relate). Level 3 — Soft Action CTA (gentle nudge). Level 4 — Direct Conversion (only for explicit promotional briefs).

Match CTA to the content's ending emotion. If the body ended with hesitation, CTA should invite shared experience. If it ended with relief, CTA should reflect on that feeling. The CTA should feel like a natural conversation ending, not a commercial prompt.

skills.name: Sales Pressure Detector
skills.description: Detect and remove CTA language that feels like an advertisement. The CTA must not break the authentic content experience.
directives: Detect and remove CTA language that feels like an advertisement. The CTA must not break the authentic content experience.

Structure: Real Scene → Personal Feeling → Discovery → Natural Action. Never: Brand Intro → Features → CTA.
Hook Rule: First sentence must be a personal moment, not an introduction. Never start with business announcements or brand descriptions.

Selling Point Rule: Every feature must answer 'Why does this matter to a real person?' Format: Feature + User Pain + Specific Proof + Purchase Reason. Never list features as standalone facts.

FORBIDDEN Patterns: Feature-list paragraphs, brand-introduction openings, hard-sell CTAs, bilingual mixing, AI-template structures, summary-style emotions.
Environment Rule: Never list decoration details. Focus on how the space made you feel — less intimidating, more comfortable, easier to relax.
Emoji Rule: Every emoji must match the emotion of the sentence. Fear/hesitation → 😭😅, surprise → 👀✨, comfort → 🤍🧘, interaction → 👇. No random decoration emojis. No category-based emojis.
CTA Rule: One soft CTA max per post. Prioritize engagement (save/comment/share/question) over conversion (book/buy/visit). Natural placement, never a command. Match CTA to content ending emotion.
